text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat criticised Israel on Sunday for its plan to build a new settlement in Arab east Jerusalem, saying Israeli policies were bringing the Middle East peace process to a dead-end.
He told an Islamic summit in Islamabad that Israeli "obstinacy and intransigence" had frozen peace negotiations with Syria and Lebanon and hindered those with the Palestinians.

"We were surprised by the Israeli decision to isolate and Judaise Jerusalem, constructing new settlements not only inside it but outside it," Arafat told the one-day summit of the 54-member Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC).

Israeli-Palestinian tension has been high since Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Natanyahu sent bulldozers last Tuesday to a hill between Jerusalem and Bethlehem to begin a new Jewish settlement in territory occupied by Israel.
A suicide bombing, claimed by the radical Moslem Hamas group, killed three Israeli women in Tel Aviv on Friday.
Arafat accused Israel of delaying implementation of agreements with the Palestinians to "please right-wing Israeli religious parties which are hostile to the peace process".
He criticised the United States for twice vetoing a United Nations Security Council resolution demanding that Israel halt the East Jerusalem settlement.
"Unfortunately the veto of the United States, twice, only helped encourage Israel to pursue its aggression and its challenge to international legitimacy," Arafat said.
Arafat said that what he called Israel's policy of building new settlements and imposing collective punishments and economic blockades against the Palestinians was very dangerous.

"Our efforts to save the peace process and put it back on its normal track are continuous and relentless, but it requires a true partnership, it depends on the goodwill of the Israeli government to the letter and spirit of what has been agreed."

Arafat said 1993 peace accords were based on the formula of land-for-peace, but the present Israeli government had rejected this, seeking "land, peace and security" with the Arab and Islamic countries as well as with the Palestinians.
"What sort of trust and cooperation can be established in context of such an Israeli policy, derived from the arrogance of the past, the arrogance of power and occupation?" he asked.
"Peace will not become a reality unless Jerusalem is returned to its owners as capital of the state of Palestine," Arafat declared, speaking for the Arab group at the OIC.
The special OIC conference was called to help Pakistan mark its golden jubilee year, celebrating 50 years of independence.
